prompt: Our payment gateway client in the billing-service repo keeps hanging when the upstream provider blips. I wrote a custom retry loop in src/gateway_client.py three months ago, but it does not handle exponential backoff correctly and sometimes retries too fast. We need to replace this hand-rolled logic with a standard retry library while strictly maintaining our current total timeout of 4500 milliseconds. If the total time exceeds that limit, the caller in src/order_processor.py must fail immediately, not wait longer. Please draft an implementation plan that identifies the exact lines to change in the client module and lists the specific unit tests in tests/test_gateway.py that need updating to verify the new behavior. Do not just weaken the existing assertions to make them pass; we need to prove the backoff steps are correct. Ravi from the payments team says this is blocking the Q3 launch, so I need this plan by tomorrow at 10 AM. The repo is written in Python, and you can verify changes by running the command make test-gateway. Ensure the dependency on the new library does not break the build for the notification service, which imports this client.

The dashboard for our inventory management system at Northwind is timing out because the product search query in src/db_queries.sql takes nearly 8 seconds to run when we have over 50000 items. We need to add caching to this specific query to bring the response time under 200 milliseconds. However, the cache must invalidate immediately whenever a write operation occurs in the src/inventory_writer.py module, or else warehouse staff will see stale stock levels. The current test suite in tests/test_cache_layer.py has a flaky test that sometimes passes even when the cache is not cleared; do not simply disable or weaken this test to get a green build. I need a delivery plan that includes specific checks to verify cache invalidation happens within 50 milliseconds of a write. Our lead operator, Jane, warned that incorrect stock data caused a shipping error last week, so correctness is critical. The project uses TypeScript, and you can run the verification suite with npm run verify-db. Please include how we will monitor cache hit rates after deployment. I need this plan by end of day today so we can merge before the weekend traffic spike.

We are updating the default connection pool size in our core configuration file located at config/app_defaults.yaml. Currently, it is set to 20, but performance testing shows we need to increase this to 50 to handle the holiday rush. However, several of our long-running batch jobs rely on the old default value because they do not explicitly override it in their environment variables. If we change this blindly, the batch processor in src/batch_runner.js might exhaust database connections and crash. I need a delivery plan that outlines how to roll this out safely without disrupting the nightly data sync that processes 1.2 million records. Do not just update the file and hope for the best; we need a strategy to identify which services depend on the implicit default. The repo is written in JavaScript, and the full test suite runs via yarn test-all. There is a temptation to skip the integration test for the batch runner because it takes 15 minutes, but do not do that. Our operations lead, Marcus, requires a verification step that simulates high load before we merge. Please provide a split verification approach that allows us to test this in staging first. I need this by Thursday noon.

We launched the beta dark mode feature six months ago using a feature flag called enable_dark_beta, and now we want to make it the default for everyone and remove the flag entirely. The flag check exists in src/ui_theme_manager.ts and controls a code path that is now dead since we are forcing the new theme. However, the mobile app version 2.1 still sends a parameter that expects the old flag to exist, and removing it might cause those clients to crash or show a blank screen. We have about 3000 users on that old version. I need an implementation plan that details how to safely delete the flag and the associated dead code in the theme module without breaking legacy clients. Do not take the shortcut of just commenting out the flag check; we must remove the code cleanly. The repository is TypeScript-based, and you can run the test suite with npm run test:unit. Please include a check to ensure the mobile API contract remains compatible during the transition. Sarah from mobile engineering needs to sign off on this, so include a verification step she can run. The deadline is next Tuesday before the next mobile release cycle.

Our user registration form in src/signup_handler.go accepts email addresses without proper validation, leading to bounced emails and dirty data. We need to add strict input validation to this handler to ensure emails match a standard pattern and domains are not disposable. This handler is copied by three other microservices for different signup flows, so whatever pattern we implement here will likely be duplicated elsewhere. If we do this wrong, we might block legitimate users with complex but valid email addresses. I need an implementation plan that defines the validation logic and explains how to propagate this change to the other three handlers without introducing inconsistencies. Do not weaken the existing test in tests/test_signup.go that currently allows invalid emails just to avoid refactoring; instead, update the test to reflect the new strict rules. The codebase is Go, and tests run with go test ./.... Our compliance officer, David, requires that we log every rejected attempt, so include that in the plan. We have a hard deadline of Friday at 4 PM because marketing is launching a campaign that expects clean data. Please outline how we will verify that no valid emails are falsely rejected.

Once a week in production, our job queue consumer in src/queue_worker.py fails to process a batch of image resizing tasks, causing a backlog of about 200 jobs. We suspect a race condition where two workers pick up the same job ID when the queue is under heavy load, but we cannot reproduce it locally. The current test suite in tests/test_worker.py passes consistently because it runs single-threaded. We need to fix this race condition to ensure zero duplicate processing. Do not take the shortcut of adding a sleep delay to mask the timing issue; we need a proper synchronization fix. I need a delivery plan that includes a strategy for writing a concurrent test that can reliably reproduce the race condition so we can verify the fix. The project is in Python, and you can run the standard tests with pytest. Our site reliability engineer, Elena, says this backlog causes customer complaints every Saturday morning, so this is urgent. Please include a check to verify that job completion times do not degrade by more than 10 percent after the fix. I need this plan by Wednesday morning so we can deploy before the weekend peak.

We have a shared helper function for currency formatting in src/utils/formatting.js that is used by twelve different modules across our finance and checkout services. It has grown too large and now includes logic specific to the checkout flow, which makes it hard to maintain. We need to move this helper into its own standalone package and update all twelve callers to import from the new location. During this move, we must ensure that the rounding behavior for EUR transactions, which handles 3 decimal places for specific assets, does not change. If we break this, our financial reports will be off by small amounts that accumulate over time. I need an implementation plan that lists the steps to extract the package, update the imports in all callers, and verify the output matches exactly. Do not skip updating the tests in the checkout module just because they are complex; they must pass. The repo is JavaScript, and the full test command is npm run test:full. Our lead accountant, Priya, needs a verification report showing before-and-after values for a sample set of 1000 transactions. The deadline is next Monday before the month-end close.

We need to add detailed logging around the payment processing flow in src/payment_gateway.rb to help debug recent failures, but we must strictly avoid recording any personal data like credit card numbers or customer names. Currently, the logger in src/logger_util.rb does not have filters for sensitive fields, so a naive implementation might leak PII. We process about 5000 payments a day, and even one leak is unacceptable. I need a delivery plan that specifies exactly where to add logs, what data to include, and how to sanitize the output to ensure compliance. Do not take the shortcut of disabling logs in the test environment to avoid dealing with sanitization; the tests must verify that no PII is ever logged. The codebase is Ruby, and you can run the test suite with bundle exec rspec. Our security lead, Tom, requires a manual review of the log output format before merging. Please include a verification step that attempts to log a test payload containing fake credit card numbers and proves they are masked. I need this plan by Thursday at 2 PM.

Our export service generates CSV files for customers who import the data into their own ERP systems. Currently, the date format in these exports is MM/DD/YYYY, but a major client requires ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) starting next month. Changing this default in src/export_generator.java will affect all 1500 active customers, and about 200 of them have parsers that might break if the format changes unexpectedly. We need to implement this change in a way that allows us to migrate customers gradually or detect when their parsers fail. I need an implementation plan that describes how to switch the format, how to monitor for parsing errors on the client side, and how to roll back if necessary. Do not simply update the format string and ignore the risk to existing integrations; we need a mitigation strategy. The project is Java, and tests run with mvn test. Our customer success manager, Linda, says we must have a verification plan that validates the output against a set of 50 sample customer parsers. The deadline is two weeks from today to align with the client's upgrade cycle.

Our CI pipeline currently takes 45 minutes to complete, largely due to a slow integration test in tests/test_full_stack.py that spins up a real database and external services. The ticket author believes this test is redundant because unit tests already cover the logic, and they want to remove it to speed up deployments. However, this test caught a critical data corruption bug last month that unit tests missed. We need to evaluate whether we can safely remove or refactor this test without losing coverage of end-to-end behaviors. I need a delivery plan that analyzes the coverage provided by this specific test, proposes a way to speed it up or replace it with a faster equivalent, and defines checks to ensure we do not regress on the data corruption scenario. Do not just delete the test to save 10 minutes; we must prove the risk is acceptable. The repo is Python, and the CI command is make ci-run. Our engineering director, Alex, requires a comparison of bug detection rates before approving any removal. Please include a verification step that runs the old test in parallel with the new approach for one week. The deadline is next Friday.
